result.markdown: --- title: "Session 1 — Counts, Rates and the Poisson Idea" subtitle: "Counts vs rates · person-time · mean and variance · zeros · trend and season · Lab 1" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Regression workshop: continuous outcomes (linear) and yes/no outcomes (logistic) - Today: the outcome is a **count of events**: cases per ward per month, admissions per day, deaths per year - By the end you can: - tell a **count** from a **rate**, and name the right **denominator** - compute **incidence rates** and **rate ratios** from a table - describe the **Poisson** idea and check **mean vs variance** - spot **zeros**, **trend** and **seasonality** ::: ## Our data: dengue in a city ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} - **30 wards** x **36 months** (2023-2025) = 1,080 ward-months - `cases` notified, ward `population`, `slum` ward, `rain_mm`, **fogging** (vector control) in half the wards from month 25 - Invented, but built to behave like real surveillance data ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dg |> select(ward, date, population, slum, cases, rain_lag1, fogging) |> head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 ward date population slum cases rain_lag1 fogging 1 W01 2023-01-01 11300 Non-slum 2 90 No 2 W01 2023-01-31 11300 Non-slum 0 0 No 3 W01 2023-03-03 11300 Non-slum 2 0 No 4 W01 2023-04-02 11300 Non-slum 4 33 No 5 W01 2023-05-03 11300 Non-slum 5 57 No 6 W01 2023-06-02 11300 Non-slum 4 190 No ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Topic 1 — Counts and rates {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A count is not a rate ::: {.incremental} - **Count:** how many events (cases) - **Rate:** events per unit of **person-time at risk**: cases / (people x time) - A ward of 60,000 will have more cases than a ward of 8,000 **even at the same risk** - **Compare rates, not counts**, unless you only want workload ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(cases = sum(dg$cases), rate_per_100k_person_months = round(sum(dg$cases) / sum(dg$population) * 1e5, 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` cases rate_per_100k_person_months 10411.0 34.3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} dg |> group_by(slum) |> summarise(cases = sum(cases), person_months = sum(population), rate_per_100k = round(cases / person_months * 1e5, 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 4 slum cases person_months rate_per_100k 1 Non-slum 4312 16516800 26.1 2 Slum 6099 13870800 44 ``` ::: ::: ## Person-time and the rate ratio ::: {.key} **Person-time** is the denominator: each ward-month contributes its population x 1 month. The slum **rate ratio** is about 1.7. ::: # Topic 2 — The Poisson distribution {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Counts of rare, independent events ::: {.eq} P(Y = k) = e^-mu^ mu^k^ / k! with **mean = variance = mu** ::: ::: {.incremental} - Events occur **independently**, at a **constant rate**, and one at a time - The single parameter **mu** is both the **mean** and the **variance** - Skewed for small mu, nearly symmetric for large mu - Poisson regression (Session 2) models log(mu) as a linear function of predictors ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} bind_rows(tibble(k = 0:25, p = dpois(0:25, 2), mu = "mean 2"), tibble(k = 0:25, p = dpois(0:25, 10), mu = "mean 10")) |> ggplot(aes(k, p, fill = mu)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") + labs(x = "Count", y = "Probability", fill = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s1_counts_rates_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ## Does our data look Poisson? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(mean = round(mean(dg$cases), 1), variance = round(var(dg$cases), 0)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean variance 9.6 394.0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} c(observed_zeros = round(mean(dg$cases == 0), 3), poisson_expected_zeros = signif(dpois(0, mean(dg$cases)), 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` observed_zeros poisson_expected_zeros 0.202000 0.000065 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.bad} The **variance is about 41 times the mean**, and there are far more **zeros** than a Poisson allows. This is **overdispersion** (Session 3) and **excess zeros** (Session 4). Part of it is just **different wards, seasons and rates mixed together**, which regression can explain. ::: # Topic 3 — Look before you model {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Trend and seasonality ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} dg |> group_by(date) |> summarise(cases = sum(cases)) |> ggplot(aes(date, cases)) + geom_line(colour = col_navy) + geom_point() + labs(x = NULL, y = "Cases in the city per month") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s1_counts_rates_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - A clear **monsoon peak** every year, and a mild upward drift - Model it: **month** (sine and cosine, or `factor(month)`) and a **time trend** - Ignoring season confounds comparisons: fogging started in **month 25**, after growth ::: ## Checklist before modelling counts ::: {.good} 1. Define the **event**, the **unit** (ward-month) and the **denominator** (person-time) 2. Plot the **distribution** (zeros? skew?) and the **time series** 3. Compare **mean and variance** by group 4. List the **exposures**, **confounders** (season, trend, ward type) and **clustering** (the same ward is measured 36 times) ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 1 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `counts-workshop/labs/lab1_counts.R` - totals, crude rates and a rate ratio by hand - mean vs variance, histogram, zeros against a Poisson - the city time series ::: **Time:** 30 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a380bk.h0q6ed" data-show="V2FyZCBCIGhhcyB0aGUgaGlnaGVyIHJhdGUsIDI1MCB2cyAxNTAgcGVyIDEwMCwwMDA=" data-explain="UmF0ZSA9IGNhc2VzIC8gcG9wdWxhdGlvbi4gQSBpcyAxNTAgcGVyIDEwMCwwMDAgYW5kIEIg aXMgMjUwIHBlciAxMDAsMDAwLCBzbyBCIGlzIGhpZ2hlciBkZXNwaXRlIGZld2VyIGNhc2Vz LiBDb3VudHMgcmVmbGVjdCBwb3B1bGF0aW9uIHNpemUu"} Ward A (60,000 people) reports 90 cases in a month and ward B (10,000 people) reports 25. Which statement is correct? - Ward A has the higher rate because it has more cases - The two wards have the same rate in the month - Ward B has the higher rate, 250 vs 150 per 100,000 - Rates cannot be calculated from one month of data ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a38dk8.h0qkvp" data-show="UGVyc29uLXRpbWUgYXQgcmlzaw==" data-explain="QW4gaW5jaWRlbmNlIHJhdGUgZGl2aWRlcyBldmVudHMgYnkgdGhlIHBlcnNvbi10aW1lIGR1 cmluZyB3aGljaCB0aGV5IGNvdWxkIG9jY3VyLCBzbyBncm91cHMgYW5kIHBlcmlvZHMgb2Yg ZGlmZmVyZW50IHNpemUgY2FuIGJlIGNvbXBhcmVkLg=="} What is the denominator of an incidence rate? - The number of wards - Person-time at risk - The number of cases - The number of months in the study ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a38qsy.h0qzd3" data-show="NCwgdGhlIHNhbWUgYXMgdGhlIG1lYW4=" data-explain="VGhlIGRlZmluaW5nIHByb3BlcnR5IG9mIHRoZSBQb2lzc29uIGRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvbiBpcyB2 YXJpYW5jZSA9IG1lYW4uIFJlYWwgY291bnRzIG9mdGVuIHZpb2xhdGUgdGhpcy4="} A Poisson distribution has mean 4. What is its variance? - 2, the square root of the mean - 16, the square of the mean - 4, the same as the mean - It cannot be determined without the data ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a3941o.h0rduh" data-show="T3ZlcmRpc3BlcnNpb246IG1vcmUgdmFyaWF0aW9uIHRoYW4gYSBQb2lzc29uIHByb2Nlc3Mg d291bGQgYWxsb3c=" data-explain="QSB2YXJpYW5jZSBmYXIgYWJvdmUgdGhlIG1lYW4gbWVhbnMgdGhlIGRhdGEgYXJlIG92ZXJk aXNwZXJzZWQsIG9mdGVuIGJlY2F1c2UgcmF0ZXMgZGlmZmVyIGJldHdlZW4gd2FyZHMgYW5k IHRpbWVzLCBvciBldmVudHMgY2x1c3Rlci4="} Monthly case counts have mean 9.6 and variance 394. What does this suggest? - A perfect Poisson process, in which variance and mean coincide - A fault in the dates in the file, which should be corrected first - That the counts are too small for any model to be fitted to them - Overdispersion: more variation than a Poisson process would allow ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a39haa.h0rsbr" data-show="SXQgc2hvd3Mgc2Vhc29uIGFuZCB0cmVuZCB0aGF0IGNvdWxkIGNvbmZvdW5kIHRoZSBjb21w YXJpc29u" data-explain="U2Vhc29uIGFuZCB0cmVuZCBhZmZlY3QgdGhlIG91dGNvbWUgYW5kIG1heSBjb2luY2lkZSB3 aXRoIHRoZSBleHBvc3VyZSAoZm9nZ2luZyBzdGFydGVkIGxhdGUgaW4gdGhlIHN0dWR5KS4g U2VlaW5nIHRoZW0gZ3VpZGVzIHdoYXQgdG8gYWRqdXN0IGZvci4="} Why does a plot of cases against time matter before modelling? - It shows season and trend that could confound the comparison - It gives the p-value for the effect of the intervention directly - It removes the need for a denominator in the rate calculation - It proves that the events in the data set occur independently ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - A **count** is not a **rate**: divide by **person-time** - Poisson: **mean = variance**; check it - Look for **zeros, skew, trend and season** before modelling - **Rate ratio** = rate in one group / rate in another ::: **Next:** Session 2: Poisson regression

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
